subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A benefit of immigration for a HOST country is often:
options: Filling labour shortages and adding skills
questions.explain: Immigrants can fill gaps in the labour market and bring skills, boosting the host country's economy.

questions.q: Which factor encourages a high population density?
options: A flat, fertile area with a temperate climate
Dense tropical rainforest with poor soils
questions.explain: Flat fertile land with a moderate climate supports farming and settlement, leading to higher population densities.

questions.q: Which of these is a common challenge caused by rapid urban growth in LICs and NEEs?
options: Too few people to fill jobs
questions.explain: Rapid growth can overwhelm services such as water, sanitation and transport, leading to congestion and pollution.

questions.q: On a settlement hierarchy, which has the highest order and largest range of services?
questions.explain: Cities and conurbations sit at the top of the settlement hierarchy with the largest populations and widest range of services.

questions.q: A megacity is usually defined as a city with a population of more than:
questions.explain: A megacity is an urban area with a population of over 10 million people.

questions.q: One way to improve a squatter settlement is through 'site and service' schemes, which:
options: Provide land with basic utilities so residents can build better homes
Move all residents to rural areas
questions.explain: Site and service schemes give people a plot connected to water and electricity, allowing them to gradually self-build improved housing.

questions.q: In a typical urban land-use pattern, which area is usually found at the centre of a city?
questions.explain: The CBD is the commercial heart of a city, with shops and offices, usually located in the centre where land is most accessible.

questions.q: Population density is best defined as:
options: The number of people per unit area
The total number of people in a country
The number of births each year
questions.explain: Population density measures how many people live in a given area, usually expressed as people per square kilometre.

questions.q: Encouraging people to cycle, walk and use trams instead of cars mainly helps a city by:
questions.explain: Integrated, low-carbon transport reduces congestion and air pollution, making the city more sustainable.

questions.q: The 'site' of a settlement refers to:
options: Its position relative to other places
The actual land on which it is built
questions.explain: Site describes the physical land a settlement is built on, while situation describes its position relative to surroundings.

options: An increasing proportion of people living in towns and cities
The growth of forests around cities
A fall in the world's total population
People moving from cities to the countryside
questions.explain: Urbanisation is the increase in the proportion of a country's population living in urban areas.

options: The population exceeds the resources available to support it
There are too few people to use resources fully
A country has lots of empty land
Birth and death rates are equal
questions.explain: Overpopulation is when the number of people exceeds the resources and technology available to maintain a good standard of living.
